Third Bail Application under Section 483 of Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 has been filed on behalf of the Applicant/Petitioner Heera Kumar Mehto seeking Bail in FIR No. 0047/2018 dated 04.03.2018 under Section 376 IPC read with Section 6 of the POCSO Act, 2012, registered at PS: Sagarpur.

2. It is submitted that the Supreme Court vide Order dated 18.03.2024 passed in Special Leave to Appeal (Criminal) No.3726/2024 dismissed the Bail Application filed on behalf of the Applicant with liberty to file the same before the learned Trial Court after six month.
It is also submitted present Application has been filed since more than 06 months have passed.
3. The Applicant is stated to be in Judicial Custody for 07 years and 05 months.
All Prosecution witnesses already stand recorded and the case is pending for the recording of statement of the Applicant.
It is further submitted that age of the prosecutrix is seriously disputed.

sentences.text: It is even further asserted that it is the case where the relationship was consensual, as is brought out as per the testimony of witnesses as well as from the Status Report.
It is contended that the learned Trial Court has dismissed the Bail Application vide Order dated 21.10.2024, without considering the observations of the Hon'ble Apex Court and on insignificant facts.
The liberty of an accused is an important factor, as every accused is presumed to be innocent unless proven guilty.
He cannot be denied bail even though he has been in custody for approximately 7.5 years.
Without prejudice even if the Applicant is convicted, it would be for 7 years, he has already undergone 7 years' imprisonment and therefore is entitled to bail.
5. It is further submitted that the Prosecutrix has already married and is settled in her life.

Even the father of the Prosecutrix, who appeared before the learned Trial Court on issuance of Notice, had stated that the bail be granted to the Applicant, who is in judicial custody for such a long time.
Despite this, his Bail Application was rejected.
6. It is submitted that the Applicant is an innocent person, who has been falsely implicated in this case of rape.
FIR was registered on the basis of statement made by an NGO, it is therefore submitted that the Applicant be granted bail.
7. Status Report filed on behalf of the State, be taken on record.
It is submitted therein that DNA testing of the un-born child had matched with that of the Applicant.
There are no grounds to assume that the Complainant/ This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 05/08/2025 at 22:27:11 Prosecutrix had consented or there was consensual relationship between her and the Applicant.
As per the FIR, the age of the Complainant/Prosecutrix was 15 years and the Applicant is the husband of her sister.

She had corroborated he statements under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
8.

Bail is opposed on the ground of gravity of the offence, severity of the punishment; character,
behavior, means, position and standing of the Applicant; likelihood of the offence being repeated and the danger of the justice being thwarted by grant of bail.
9.
Submissions heard and record perused.

10. The case of the Prosecution is that the Prosecutrix was the younger sister of Applicant's wife,
who, because of relationship between them, got pregnant and the DNA of un-born child matched with that of the Applicant.
As per the Prosecution, the Prosecution evidence has been concluded and the case is at the stage of statement of the Accused.
11. Since the trial is almost at the fag end and looking at the gravity of the offence, no case is made out for grant of bail.
12. The Bail Application along with pending Application is dismissed.
